headline: GOLD FIELDS GOES HOSTILE: $27B NORTHERN STAR BATTLE HEATS UP AS NEW CEO FACES BAPTISM OF FIRE
snippet: Gold Fields launched a formal hostile takeover bid for Northern Star Resources (ASX: NST) after the Australian miner's board unanimously rejected an A$38.7 billion cash-and-scrip proposal — approximately A$23.76 per share — with investors expecting a sweetened offer weighted toward more cash following a Gold Fields investor roadshow in Australia. Northern Star's new CEO Suresh Vadnagra officially took the helm on October 5, immediately facing pressure to articulate a standalone value case that exceeds the bid, while NST shares trade at A$25.59 — above the implied offer value — signalling the market expects Gold Fields to return with a higher number.

headline: EM&T POHANG RARE EARTH MAGNET PLANT SETS DEC. 17 SHOWCASE — 10,000-TONNE EXPANSION TARGETS DFARS 2027 DEFENSE CUTOFF
snippet: Evolution Metals & Technologies (Nasdaq: EMAT) announced a December 17 ribbon-cutting and production showcase at its Pohang, South Korea plant — currently the largest high-performance rare earth magnet facility in production outside China — as the company targets expansion to 10,000+ metric tons annually from roughly 1,000 tons today. The announcement is timed precisely to the January 1, 2027 DFARS 252.225-7052 deadline, which will bar U.S. defense contractors from sourcing magnets from China and other covered nations, creating immediate procurement urgency for defence, automotive, and unmanned-systems buyers.

headline: TRUMP SEALS $120B NUCLEAR REACTOR PACT WITH SOUTH KOREA — 8 REACTORS (SIX AP1000, TWO APR1400) IN PROJECT POWER
snippet: The Trump administration unveiled a $200 billion South Korean energy investment package with $120 billion earmarked for eight large-scale nuclear reactors on U.S. soil — six Westinghouse AP1000 units plus two South Korean APR1400 designs — under a framework called Project Power, alongside $54 billion for Alaska LNG and $22 billion for a Texas gas-fired data-centre plant. The nuclear program is part of Seoul's $350 billion commitment to U.S. investment in exchange for tariff relief, though each reactor still requires NRC approval and Seoul has flagged that the Alaska LNG commitment is subject to commercial viability review.

headline: FREEPORT Q3: 830M LBS COPPER DELIVERED ON PLAN — GRASBERG SMELTER BACK ONLINE AFTER LATE AUGUST RESTART
snippet: Freeport-McMoRan (NYSE: FCX) reported third-quarter 2026 consolidated copper production of approximately 830 million pounds — in line with management expectations — with marginally better international results offsetting slightly lower U.S. output, while PTFI's Grasberg copper smelter successfully restarted in late August, normalising Indonesia operations after earlier disruption. Gold output reached approximately 230,000 ounces, also in line with guidance, and copper sales for Q3 are projected at 750 million pounds, consistent with FCX's July estimate.

headline: SILVER MINERS TRADE AT 30% OF HISTORICAL NAV — 67-MILLION-OZ ANNUAL DEFICIT MAKES THIS THE BEST CONTRARIAN ENTRY IN YEARS
snippet: Despite silver trading near $62/oz against a structural 67 million-ounce annual supply deficit — the sixth consecutive year of shortfalls per the Silver Institute — silver mining equities are valued at roughly 30% of their historical relationship to net asset value, a dislocation the analysis argues creates an asymmetric setup heading into the October 27-28 FOMC meeting. The core thesis: market-wide scepticism that $50+ silver can persist is actively suppressing equity valuations even as miners generate free cash flow at multiples of 2020 levels, with silver equities offering more mispricing potential than gold miners right now.

headline: EVERGOLD GL26-031: 4.9M AT 7.70 G/T GOLD + 186 G/T SILVER IN BC TOODOGGONE — LEAD-ZINC ASSAYS STILL PENDING
snippet: Evergold Corp. released initial results from the first six 2026 drill holes at the GL1 Zone of its Golden Lion project in northern British Columbia's Toodoggone mining district, with hole GL26-031 returning 4.9 metres at 7.70 g/t gold and 186.0 g/t silver from an epithermal-style system. Lead and zinc assays from the same holes remain pending, meaning the metal equivalent grade — and commercial width of the interval — may improve materially when the full polymetallic suite is available.

headline: XCITE URANIUM DRILLS BLACK BAY FOR FIRST TIME — HISTORIC FLOAT SAMPLES HIT 7.37% U3O8 AT URANIUM CITY, SASK.
snippet: Xcite Uranium Inc., partnered with Eagle Plains Resources (TSX-V: EPL), commenced the first-ever drill program at the Black Bay Project in Uranium City, Saskatchewan, following 2026 fieldwork that returned historic trenching up to 1.17% U3O8 and a Brunston Zone float sample grading 7.37% U3O8. The maiden holes target subsurface continuity beneath surface occurrences along a uranium trend in the Athabasca Basin fringe, one of the world's highest-grade uranium regions.

headline: CANADIAN GOLDFIELDS LAUNCHES FALL PROGRAM AT MIMINISKA — 14KM GOLD TREND, 12KM LARGELY UNDRILLED IN NW ONTARIO
snippet: Canadian Goldfields Discovery Corp. (TSX-V: CGM) launched its 2026 fall program at the Miminiska Gold Project in northwestern Ontario, comprising approximately 1,500 soil samples and an airborne magnetic survey designed to vector drill targets across a 14-kilometre iron-formation trend with roughly 12 kilometres of prospective strike between the Miminiska and Frond Zones that remains essentially untested by historical drilling. The program advances in partnership with Eabametoong First Nation and sets the stage for a winter drill campaign at what the company calls a high-grade, district-scale gold system.

headline: GALWAY METALS DRILLS DEEPER AT CLARENCE STREAM SOUTHWEST — 1.42-MOZ SYSTEM EXTENDS BELOW CURRENT RESOURCE ENVELOPE
snippet: Galway Metals (TSX-V: GWM) released new drill results from its Southwest Deposit at the Clarence Stream Gold Project in New Brunswick, demonstrating that high-grade gold mineralization continues below the envelope that underpins the current 1.42-million-ounce indicated resource. The 2026 program has returned results including 2.0 g/t gold over 68 metres and 2.6 g/t gold over 48 metres at Southwest, with five rigs running a 75,000-metre campaign aimed at supporting a pre-feasibility study decision.

headline: UR-ENERGY: WYOMING URANIUM AT $50-55/LB ALL-IN — CUSTOMERS NOW CHOOSING SUPPLY SECURITY OVER PRICE AT $97 SPOT
snippet: At Mining Forum Americas 2026, Ur-Energy (TSX: URE) detailed an all-in operating cost structure of $50–$55 per pound — well below the current uranium term price of $97 per pound — as it expands Wyoming in-situ recovery operations and targets third mine construction at Ludeman. Management reported a structural shift in customer behaviour: utilities and government buyers are now prioritising domestic supply chain security over spot price optimisation, a dynamic Ur-Energy says will sustain premium pricing for U.S. producers through the current demand cycle.
